topics.title: How evidence is checked
topics.why: Different reports can describe the same trial. A source can be independent and still have methodological weaknesses.
topics.question: Which findings are original, replicated, conflicting, or simply a hypothesis?
compare: Original research
Look for methods, comparators, denominators and outcomes.
Unpublished or informal sources
Use trial registries, preprints, theses and media to find evidence or questions; check original data.
Safety and funding
Check sponsor involvement separately from risk of bias. An unknown disclosure is not evidence of independence.
topics.pending: Full claim-to-source verification, independent reviewer and a structured media search beyond this initial example.

topics.title: Development across the weeks
topics.why: Organs and functions mature across overlapping time windows. A week number is a navigation reference, not a test of normal development.
topics.question: What is changing around this time, and how is it assessed?
compare: Stage reference
Use gestational age and source windows rather than an exact milestone deadline.
Biology vs intervention
Understanding a developing organ does not establish that a supplement or stimulation changes its outcome.
Clinical assessment
A clinical visit or test answers a different question from an educational milestone chart.
topics.pending: Individual week-level claim and source locator review, visual accuracy and clinician-approved urgent guidance.

topics.title: Nutrients: adequacy and disputed benefits
topics.why: Nutrients have essential biological roles, but an adequate intake reference is not a therapeutic dose. Population intake gaps do not diagnose an individual deficiency.
topics.question: Do supplements improve a meaningful pregnancy outcome beyond adequate dietary intake?
compare: 2018 omega-3 review
Early preterm birth reduction reported across included trials.
2019 ORIP trial
No clear reduction in its studied population; interval includes both benefit and harm.
Interpretation
Different populations, baseline intake and regimens; trial registry links exploratory analyses to the original cohort. No universal supplemental dose inferred.
topics.pending: Food portions, bioavailability, deficiency diagnosis vs population gaps, age/stage reference intake review, updated pooled evidence and trial-level funding.

topics.title: Skin and stretch marks
topics.why: Moisturizing comfort, prevention of new striae, and treatment of established striae are separate outcomes.
topics.question: Does a specific formulation prevent stretch marks compared with a suitable control?
compare: Creams and oils
No high-quality preventive evidence in the older review; this does not rule out every formulation.
Massage and traditional preparations
Investigate product-specific trials and harms rather than assume benefit from anecdote.
Existing marks
Separate postpartum appearance and function outcomes; pregnancy safety must be established for any treatment.
topics.pending: Product/ingredient trials, confounding, sponsor donations, new prevention studies, treatment-specific safety and rights-cleared visuals.

topics.title: Movement, pelvic floor and recovery
topics.why: Muscle strength, pain, leakage and anatomical spacing are different outcomes. Progression should not be inferred from a calendar alone.
topics.question: Which outcomes improve with a studied exercise intervention, and which remain uncertain?
compare: Pelvic floor
Prevention and treatment studies involve different populations.
Abdominal training
Smaller inter-rectus distance is not proof of restored function or a particular appearance.
Symptoms and harms
Pain, overactivity, prolapse and recovery after delivery require individualized assessment; no universal exercise protocol.
topics.pending: Independent review of updated 2026 review, trials and adverse events, safe stage-specific video demos, function and pain outcomes.

topics.title: Preparation for both parents
topics.why: Fertility biomarkers and live birth are not interchangeable. Maternal folate prevention evidence is distinct from supplements marketed for male infertility.
topics.question: Does a proposed preparation intervention improve pregnancy or live birth, rather than only a laboratory marker?
compare: Male fertility supplement trial
Folic acid plus zinc showed no clear live-birth or semen-quality benefit in its infertility-treatment population.
Lifestyle intervention
Compare the timing of care, eligibility and outcomes; avoid imposing a universal body-size or delay requirement.
Shared preparation
Use the three-year horizon to organize reading and questions, not claim an optimal cosmetic regimen.
topics.pending: Paternal exposures, semen and live-birth evidence with retraction-dependent results excluded; compare fertility treatments, health history and medication review.

topics.title: Plastics, food and household exposure
topics.why: A chemical level in urine is an exposure marker, not automatically a measurement of disease or fetal harm.
topics.question: Can a practical change reduce a measured exposure, and is there evidence of improved health?
compare: 2026 PERTH pilot
Selected urinary plastic-associated biomarkers fell after a short intervention in adults.
2013 dietary trial
Unexpected DEHP increases from food contamination challenge the assumption that low-packaging meals guarantee lower exposure.
Interpretation
Compounds, sources, study population and endpoints differ. Avoid assigning an arbitrary toxicity score or claiming a fetal benefit.
Water filter claims
Compare the exact model, certified contaminant and replacement schedule rather than relying on a broad claim of purification. EPA notes limits to what certification alone establishes.
topics.pending: PFAS, water filters, pesticides, cosmetics, air and occupational exposures; realistic costs, individual source attribution and direct pregnancy health outcomes.

topics.title: Infant feeding, eczema & allergy
topics.why: Feeding methods, eczema prevention, food allergy and growth are distinct outcomes. An intervention may have different effects on each.
topics.question: Do popular infant care practices improve the specific outcome they claim to improve?
compare: Eczema prevention

BEEP did not demonstrate prevention with daily emollient in high-risk infants and reported a skin infection signal. PreventADALL also found no preventive effect for its studied skin intervention at 12 months.
Food allergy is a different outcome
PreventADALL reported fewer food allergy diagnoses in its food-intervention groups. The new seven-year follow-up needs separate appraisal before claims about durable effects.
Baby-led feeding

BLISS studied a supported, modified approach rather than unsupervised feeding. No clear choking difference or improved body weight was established. A separate 2023 trial also examined modified methods with safety guidance.
Research boundaries
Do not turn trial age ranges into home feeding instructions. Individual readiness, choking prevention, allergy risk and existing eczema treatment need distinct assessment.
topics.pending: Full trial-level funding and conflicts, exact outcome extraction, recent follow-up, independent reviews, feeding readiness and safety, elimination communication, sleep and family experience research.

topics.title: Pregnancy folklore: what has been tested?
topics.why: Long-standing observations can be worth examining. An association may be real without being a useful individual prediction.
topics.question: Which familiar beliefs have human data?
compare: Heartburn and newborn hair
A small study found a moderate association; 23 of 28 with moderate or severe heartburn had babies with average or above-average hair. The mechanism was not demonstrated.
Baby's sex and symptoms
Some symptom patterns differ on average by fetal sex, but overlap is substantial. Abdominal shape and symptoms are not reliable sex tests.
topics.pending: Replicate findings, inspect exact full texts, search ethnographic and historical literature; no unsupported claims.

topics.title: Traditional approaches to pregnancy nausea
topics.why: Symptom relief, vomiting prevention, hydration and pregnancy safety are separate outcomes.
topics.question: What has been tested beyond standard medicines?
compare: Ginger
A recent review found a possible reduction in nausea on one scale, with low confidence; another symptom scale produced inconsistent results.
Acupressure
Sham comparisons do not establish prevention. Investigate individual symptom outcomes and blinding separately.
Aromatherapy
Small inhalation trials deserve review, but findings cannot be generalized to oral oils, all products or long-term safety. One trial had commercial formulation assistance.
topics.pending: Full trial funding, product identity, symptoms/harms and retraction checks; no self-treatment protocol; persistent or severe vomiting needs assessment.

topics.title: Traditional birth preparation & labor comfort
topics.why: Long-used physical techniques and foods have different evidence bases. Comfort is not the same as preventing injury or initiating birth.
topics.question: Which low-cost practices have direct human evidence?
compare: Perineal massage
Older antenatal review found fewer injuries requiring sutures and fewer episiotomies. Labor massage is a different intervention.
Warm compresses
Older pooled results favored fewer combined severe tears; later review estimates for individual tear grades were very imprecise.
Dates and raspberry leaf
Dates have suggestive but heterogeneous evidence. Raspberry leaf has weak evidence and conflicting observational associations; one newer study reports no outside funding, not absence of bias.
Midwifery media
Podcast and NCT article provide discovery leads, not extra independent trials. Original sources and limits are linked.
topics.pending: No home induction or herb schedule; verify contraindications and safety with qualified reviewers. Investigate other cultural and midwifery traditions.

topics.title: Traditional postpartum comfort & recovery
topics.why: Symptom relief, breast feeding function, healing and permanent physical changes are different outcomes.
topics.question: Can inexpensive physical practices help with specific recovery symptoms?
compare: Cabbage leaves and cooling
Small evidence base suggests possible pain relief during engorgement. No proof of improved supply or treatment of infection.
Abdominal binding
Two reviews in 2021 reached differing postoperative pain findings; updated evidence examines interference with breastfeeding. No proof of permanent shaping or healing diastasis.
Practical implications
These are outcome-specific research questions, not a protocol. New or worsening postpartum symptoms should be assessed.
topics.pending: Reconcile trial overlap, timing, clinically meaningful pain changes, safety and device supply funding; investigate culturally specific practices separately.

topics.title: Traditional childhood remedies: benefit and safety
topics.why: Young children are not small adults. A traditional product may have a positive symptom trial but insufficient safety evidence.
topics.question: Which remedies have evidence, and which remain unsafe or unverified?
compare: Infant colic and fennel

A positive older trial is a research lead, not a recommendation. Reviews identified serious limitations; a 2025 EFSA draft raised safety concerns for vulnerable groups. Do not administer fennel oil or herbal preparations to an infant based on this evidence.
Honey for cough

Some short-term benefit has been reported for children aged at least one year. Trial funding includes honey-industry and pharmaceutical interests. Never give honey to a child younger than 12 months because of botulism risk.
Family experiences
Reports of improvement matter as experiences, but natural recovery and differences in severity can make cause difficult to establish.
topics.pending: Current pediatric safety and full disclosures, additional independent reviews and qualitative caregiver accounts; no infant dosing or unsafe self-treatment.
